item.title: Steph Curry shooting left-handed? Warriors' Brandin Podziemski made it happen to improve his game
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski reacts after a three-point basket against the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of an NBA Cup basketball game, Saturday, Oct. 30, 2026, in San Francisco. (Justine Willard/Associated Press) As Brandin Podziemski huddled with his personal trainer this past summer, exploring how to raise his game, they hit on some ideas. They watched video of New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson, freshly crowned NBA champion. They examined the 3-point shooting volume of players such as Payton Pritchard and Tyler Herro. At some point, Podziemski posed a simple if heavy question: What about Steph? Stephen Curry counts as a model of efficient movement and basketball creativity. And the trainer, Dustin VanLieu, knew exactly how to help Podziemski gain deeper insight from his decorated Golden State Warriors teammate – magically make Curry left-handed. VanLieu flipped videos of Curry – let's pause here for a nod to the power of digital editing tools – to turn No. 30 into a mirrored version of himself. That allowed Podziemski, who is lefty, to study the footwork, ball-handling and shot creation of a left-handed Steph Curry. The images are striking, as Curry scurries around the court like a familiar if semi-fictional character. He dribbles around bewildered opponents, as usual – even dropping Luka Doncic to the hardwood, on what looks like the opposite end of the court than the real-life moment Oct. 30 – but the sight of Curry launching long-range shots with his left hand is strangely captivating. Curry wasn't aware of Podziemski's uncommon preparation until the Chronicle showed him a video after Saturday night's overtime victory over Orlando. Curry intently watched the lefty version of himself for a few moments, then said simply, "That's crazy!" He also acknowledged the logic behind the idea. "Very creative and clever," Curry said. "It makes a lot of sense to see footwork the way he moves, to create space in a way that makes sense to him. That's pretty cool." This was not the only tool Podziemski used in the offseason, merely the most novel. The early returns suggest his work is paying dividends: He's averaging 16.3 points and 4.2 assists, while shooting better than 40% on 6.9 attempts per game from long distance – all surpassing his career highs – entering Wednesday night's road trip opener in Houston. It's just 11 games into the season, but Podziemski clearly is building on the gains he made in last season's final two-plus months, when Curry was sidelined by a knee injury. Now, with Curry back and playing at his customary elite level and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg providing fresh life, the Warriors find themselves rolling along, with eight consecutive wins. Podziemski, still just 23 years old and nearly five months younger than Lendeborg, has become a central piece of the puzzle. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: David Warner starts fresh Sandpapergate row after Graeme Hick rejects Khawaja's dressing-room claims
item.description: The infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja, triggering a war of words between former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick and David Warner. While Hick has strongly rejected Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper, Warner has hit back at the former coach, questioning his appointment and bringing Michael Di Venuto into the debate. What did Graeme Hick say about Khawaja's claims? Hick, who was part of Australia's coaching staff during the 2018 South Africa tour, described Khawaja's allegations as "absolutely false". He maintained that he had no knowledge of any discussions about using sandpaper and only became aware of the incident after seeing the footage on the big screen in Cape Town. Khawaja had claimed that the entire dressing room was aware of the ball-tampering, suggesting that responsibility for the incident went beyond the three players who were eventually punished. Warner responded by taking aim at Hick's appointment as Australia's batting coach, bringing former assistant coach Michael Di Venuto into the discussion. In response to an X post on the interview, Warner wrote: "Let's get the facts straight. Graeme Hick was only appointed because Cricket Australia was unwilling to pay Michael Di Venuto what he deserved. As players, we valued Michael so highly that we even offered to contribute from our own salaries to retain him. These discussions were taking place during the New Zealand tour. That alone speaks volumes about how highly we regarded him and how determined we were to keep him involved. Adds to why Graeme has spoken!!" — davidwarner31 (@davidwarner31) Why has the 2018 Sandpapergate controversy resurfaced? The latest exchange follows the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, in which the Australia batter revisited the events of the 2018 South Africa tour. His account has reopened questions about how much the dressing room knew about the ball-tampering incident and whether the original investigation captured the full extent of what happened. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball using a piece of sandpaper. The incident became known as Sandpapergate and led to major sanctions against the players involved. Warner and then Australia captain Steve Smith were handed one-year suspensions by Cricket Australia, while Bancroft received a nine-month ban. The episode also led to widespread criticism of Australian cricket and prompted questions about the team's culture and leadership.

item.title: 2027 Masters: Austin Smotherman still fighting for Augusta invite despite back-to-back fall wins
item.description: What a year 2026 has been for Austin Smotherman. He welcomed his third daughter into the world after contending at the Cognizant Classic earlier in the year . He made his first major championship start at Aronimink a few months later. Not discouraged from the missed cut at the PGA Championship, the 32-year-old Smotherman won for the first time in his 100th start on Tour at the Bank of Utah Championship. He didn't let the time between career win No. 1 and No. 2 last very long. Three weeks later in Bermuda, Smotherman stood in the winner’s circle again after ousting Seamus Power in a two-man playoff after weather cut the tournament short to 54 holes. With all that, his playing status secured through 2029. And now, one more mountain to climb: Finish inside the top 50 of the Official World Golf Ranking. If he clinches that before the end of the season, the No. 51-ranked Smotherman will get his first-ever invite to Augusta National. There's some risk involved — two missed cuts could theoretically send him down, outside the top 60 in the FedExCup fall points and lose his spot in the first two signature events of 2027. It's a bet Smotherman is willing to take considering the possible reward. "Do our best to put up good weeks and earn some more World Ranking points and cap off the fall hopefully on a high note," he said at his press conference at this week’s Austin Championship when asked about his plan for the next couple of weeks. "Can't take away what we did," Smotherman added. "If we miss two cuts coming up, still doing a lot well and it was the best decision I think to go give it a run. The world ranking points system, I don't understand it perfectly, that's for my team to tell me what's going on. I'm just going to go play golf." Smotherman, who turned pro in 2016 and played in Latin America the following year, credited the experience from traveling the world for helping him land where he is ahead of the season-finale tournament in Georgia next week. "I feel like my good's been good enough to have a chance to win out here for a long time," the back-to-back winner said. "I made a bunch of cuts, I've had stretches of a lot of missed cuts, I feel like I've done everything in between," he added. item.title: Jets insider savagely dunks on Aaron Glenn’s ‘on the cusp’ claim after quiet trade deadline
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Jets insider savagely dunks on Aaron Glenn’s ‘on the cusp’ claim after quiet trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets were not buyers at the NFL trade deadline this year. New York was active, but only to ship off Andre Cisco to Detroit . The Jets do not look like a playoff team this year, but should they have tried harder to add talent at the trade deadline? Jets head coach Aaron Glenn explained why the team did not make any moves at the deadline this year. “Listen, we’re not going to hide from the fact that we’re 2-7. We own that, but, man, we’re still working our asses off to make sure we fix that. We feel like we like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that,” Glenn said on Wednesday, per ESPN’s Rich Cimini. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Glenn also explained why he thinks New York is “on the cusp” despite their terrible record. “When you look at the seven losses, and this is just the facts — five of the teams (are) playoff-caliber teams. I think five of them were one-score games. I think two (of the losses were) three points, one five-point and two seven points.” However, Cimini was quick to note that New York has played the 23rd hardest schedule this season, per ESPN analytics. Even if the Jets are playing their opponents closely, they’re still losing games. It is certainly fair to point out that the Jets are still a long way from being a contender. But that could all change during the 2027 offseason. The Jets will have three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. If everything breaks their way, New York could even have three picks in the top 10. Not only could they find a franchise quarterback, but they could also add a few blue-chip players as well. The future is bright for the Jets, but it is still frustrating to see them take a passive approach to the trade deadline. Regardless, next up for New York is a Week 10 home game against Buffalo. item.title: Why USC's perfectionism might be their greatest asset––and liability
item.description: USC players celebrate a made basket during a Big Ten college basketball game against the College of Charleston, Tuesday, November 10, 2026 in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES –– Perfection is cruel, and Sitaya Fagan is learning the harsh reality of excellence. Fagan checked out of the game with minutes left in the fourth quarter, plopped into her chair, and cried. USC led 101-44. 57 points. The USC Trojans defeated the Charleston Cougars 105-44, but the story rests in the palms that held the face of the woman who went 0-for-7. The boulder-sized lump sat in her throat and chest, heavy and immovable, refusing to accept the scoreboard's narrative. Perfection is the culmination of habits amalgamated when nobody's watching. Intensity. Focus. Dedication. Efficiency. This is what USC is building. Jazzy Davidson found Fagan first, wrapped an arm around her and whispered in her ear. I've been there," Davidson said later. "We expect greatness out of all of us and being a perfectionist—it makes her who she is, but there's also a downside to that." The downside. The stone. The tears after a blowout. If you want to understand this USC team, start there. Start with a kid from Australia, miles away from the comforts of home, family and friends, crying over missed shots in a game her team led by 35 at halftime. Start with the feeling that her nine rebounds, three blocks, and two steals meant nothing because the ball wouldn't go through the net. That's not weakness. That's the obverse of the same coin that has Davidson shooting 75% on the season. It's fanatical. It's almost grandiloquent in its devotion. It's the kind of maniacal obsession that either makes championships or breaks them. In Greek mythology, three sisters controlled the threads of life. Clotho spun it. Lachesis measured it. Atropos cut it. USC has a trio holding the threads of a national championship. item.description: Aug 17, 2025; Indianapolis,IN, United States; Patrick Reed of 4 Aces GC tips his hat to the crowd after being announced during the final round of LIV Golf Indianapolis. Mandatory Credit: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun Patrick Reed has revealed his major goals for 2027 after securing his return to the PGA Tour following his departure from LIV Golf. The American wants to return to the winners’ circle, get back into the top 10 of the world rankings and earn a place on the United States Ryder Cup team. Reed discussed his plans ahead of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, where he also spoke about what representing his country again would mean to him. He has not played in a Ryder Cup since 2018 but hopes his return to the PGA Tour will give him another opportunity to compete for Team USA. The 2018 Masters champion has already secured his PGA Tour card for 2027 after finishing among the top 10 eligible players in the Race to Dubai standings. He currently sits third ahead of the final tournament of the DP World Tour season. ALSO REAAD: Bryson DeChambeau Breaks Silence After LIV Golf 2.0 Collapse With Message to Fans Reed Sets Major PGA Tour Goal After LIV Golf Exit Reed wants to return to the level he was playing at before leaving the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2022. He believes getting back to winning tournaments and improving his world ranking will be important parts of his plans for next season. “Go out and get back to the winners’ circle on the PGA Tour like I was right before I left… Go out there and assert myself into the top ten in the world again,” Reed said. The American has already won twice on the DP World Tour this season, claiming the Hero Dubai Desert Classic and Qatar Masters. Those results helped him secure his PGA Tour return through the Race to Dubai standings. Reed will now have another opportunity to compete against some of the best players in the world when he returns to the PGA Tour next year. He also hopes to get back to the form that helped him reach a career-high sixth in the world rankings. item.title: Oregon's Lanning delivers KO response to Michigan's Whittingham
item.description: Two days after Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said that Oregon coach Dan Lanning has “$50-plus million” to build a football team, Lanning responded with a dig. Lanning 1, Whittingham 0. More: 'Regression' led to Jason Beck's firing as Michigan offensive coordinator More: Should Kyle Whittingham get another season to turn things around at UM? | Take our poll The coaches will face each other on Saturday, Nov. 14, when Michigan plays at Oregon’s Autzen Stadium. Michigan is 5-4, 2-4 Big Ten, while Oregon is 6-3, 4-2. “Outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach,” Whittingham said Monday, Nov. 9, on the “Inside Michigan Football” radio show, referring to Lanning. “Tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting. It doesn’t hurt that you have $50-plus million at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. That’s not his fault. That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. “NIL is really the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much. It used to be the facilities you had, the tradition, all these other things. And now it’s, ‘Well, this is all great. But these guys have got 100 grand more for me.’ So, that’s a little bit of a factor to say the least. Not to take anything away from Dan because he is an outstanding recruiter.” Michigan reportedly has a budget of $40 million for its roster. Lanning, at his news conference on Wednesday, Nov. 11, was asked about Whittingham’s comments regarding Oregon’s budget. "Man, I've got nothing to say to Coach Whitt other than I think he's an unbelievable coach," Lanning told reporters. “And I get it — they're spending more money on the coaches they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players, but I know they've signed a couple guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player, I don't know. But Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He's a Hall of Fame coach. I've got nothing but respect for him." Lanning’s not-so-subtle reference was to Whittingham’s firing of offensive coordinator Jason Beck last Sunday, Nov. 8, after nine games. Michigan owes Beck nearly $10 million after being fired in the first-year of a three-year contract. item.description: Not many had high hopes for the Golden State Warriors this season, not with Jimmy Butler (and Moses Moody ) set to miss so much time as they recover from their respective injuries. And yet the team currently sits at 8-3, sixth overall in the West, and the deeper numbers - Golden State ranks No. 2 in offensive efficiency in 2026-27 and No. 11 in defensive efficiency - also support their hot start. On the other hand, this season, the Warriors are currently hitting 43.6 percent of their threes that NBA.com labels as wide open, the second-best mark in the league, so it's fair to wonder about the sustainability of that number. We think Stephen Curry will continue hitting his threes at a high clip, obviously, but will De'Anthony Melton , Will Richard , Al Horford and Brandin Podziemski keep shooting between 42.9 and 40.3 percent from three? That remains to be seen. There's another player on Golden State's roster currently scorching hot from three, and that's rookie phenom Yaxel Lendeborg . Lendeborg has been nothing short of a revelation for the Warriors, a breath of fresh air in a skilled 6-foot-9 package who can score from all three levels, rebound, create and defend, and who is looking like an absolute steal for Golden State, who got him with the 11th pick in the most recent draft. Absolutely no one expected Lendeborg to be as good as he is right away in the Association, as evidenced by the fact that his own college head coach at Michigan, Dusty May , didn't force the current team he's coaching, the Dallas Mavericks, to draft him with the team's ninth pick. And yet, here we are, with Lendeborg playing like an All-Star in his first season and helping carry the Warriors to an impressive start. The former Michigan standout is averaging 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game on 52.3 percent shooting from the floor and 44.3 percent shooting from three so far this season. item.description: LAS VEGAS — There is probably one arm in the Giants’ organization with the trust and the track record to handle the ninth inning. item.description: Sean McVay delivered a mix bag of news Wednesday regarding injuries to the team's top two receivers. Davante Adams could be back sooner than expected from a hamstring injury. Puka Nacua, meanwhile, will remain sidelined for a "significant period of time" with knee and toe injuries. McVay: Adams' return to face Chiefs 'realistic' McVay announced the updates while speaking with reporters. Per McVay, Adams is on track to return on the early end of his 6-10 week injury timeline and could be back as soon as Week 13 for a showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs. "We're optimistic Davante's return is sooner than later, which is a big deal to us," McVay said, per the Associated Press . McVay went on to say that a return for Adams after Week 12 against the Packers would be "a realistic timeline for us." If that timeline holds true, that means Adams will miss two more games with a ruptured hamstring that he sustained in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams face the Cardinals again on Sunday, then have a Week 11 bye before facing the Packers in Week 12. An early return would be big for a Rams team that's currently down its top two weapons in the passing game. Nacua won't go on IR, but not expected back soon Nacua sustained sprains to the MCL and PCL in his right knee and a turf toe injury in Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders. The Rams announced Monday that they expected to place the All-Pro receiver on injured reserve with the injuries. McVay said Wednesday that Nacua won't go on injured reserve, but only due to "some semantics with the roster." "He's still going to be out for a significant period of time," McVay said. What that timeline is precisely remains unclear, but McVay indicated that it could be at or beyond the minimum four-game absence required by placement on injured reserve. Davante Adams, left, is expected to return sooner from injury than Puka Nacua. Nacua was expected to miss significant time, and nothing there has changed. That the Rams could get Adams back for the stretch run of the playoff race is a win. The long end of his initial timeline would have placed him back for Week 17 and the last two games of the regular season. If he returns against the Chiefs and stays healthy, he'd be available for the last six games of the season, providing Matthew Stafford with a top-shelf target in the passing game. A six-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro, Adams was putting up Pro Bowl numbers prior to his injury. In six games, he tallied 30 catches for 480 yards and 4 touchdowns. If he returns in Week 13, he'll do so as the clear No. 1 option in the passing game as long as Nacua remains sidelined. item.title: Reds offseason plans take hit with Emilio Pagán signing with Detroit
item.description: LAS VEGAS – The Cincinnati Reds ' impossible-dream offseason just got a lot tougher with the Detroit Tigers ' $11.5 million signing of free agent Reds closer Emilio Pagán . The one-year agreement, which comes three weeks before an anticipated MLB labor lockout, also includes a bonus package. Until the deal was struck, the Reds were keeping in touch with Pagán for a possible return since declining a $10 million option for 2027 less than two weeks ago. Manager Terry Francona said as recently as Nov. 6 during a radio interview that he held out hope that Pagán would return. Pagán, 35, converted all 19 save chances with a 1.88 ERA after returning from a severe hamstring injury for the final three months of the season. He became the Reds' closer in April 2025 and earned a career-high 32 saves with a 2.88 ERA on the way to the playoffs that year. “I loved having him. He was great,” team president Nick Krall said of the veteran who was valued almost as much for his clubhouse influence as his high-level performance on the mound. “He’s been really good for us the last three, four years.” One of the reasons a return seemed plausible when Pagán opted out of his Reds contract was that he returned as a free agent a year ago after his original two-year, $16 million deal with the Reds expired. Both sides said the door was open to return and continued a dialogue. The Reds went from that playoff berth in 2025 to last place this year, their hitters striking out more and scoring less than anyone else in the league, their pitchers walking more than anyone else and their fielding ranking among the worst in the majors. Now they have to add a closer to a laundry list of needs to fill to have any semblance of a chance to return to the playoffs – which they continue to say is their goal. Krall looks like he's working without a net in that effort. He's definitely working without a payroll budget, which he said has not been determined as he spoke in Las Vegas this week during MLB's annual GM meetings. So where does all of that put the Reds’ thinking when it comes to the enormous ninth-inning hole in their pitching staff? Try to fill it specifically with an acquisition during an uncertain winter? Throw a bunch of arms into a spring competition and see where it lands? “Obviously you’d love to build the bullpen from the back forward,” Krall said. “But it’s something we’re just going to work through this offseason, and we’ll do the best we can.” This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Reds offseason plans take hit with Emilio Pagán signing with Detroit
